prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics: Newtonian concept of force as interaction (actio = reactio); reduction of force systems, cutting principle, continuum concept, stress concept, mass geometry (moments of inertia, deviation moments, inertia tensor).

Basic knowledge of mathematics: vector algebra, linear equations, trigonometry (trigonometric functions); fundamentals of differential calculus (derivatives and integration rules of elementary functions, curve discussion); solution of simple, mostly linear ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients.
Open approach to new, often complex relationships.

Successful completion of either the exercise 'Mathematik 1 für MB, WIMB und VT' (3,0/2,0 UE) or the lecture 'Mathematik 1 für MB, WIMB und VT' (6,0/4,0 VO) is required to attend the exercise 'Mechanik 2' (3,0/3,0 UE).
Successful completion of the exercise 'Mechanik 2' (3,0/3,0 UE) is required to take the exam for the lecture 'Mechanik 2' (5,0/3,0 VO).

learning_outcomes.text: Calculate velocity and acceleration of arbitrary system points of a kinematic chain with joints relative to different reference systems as a function of given position coordinates and their derivatives, and represent them as vector quantities in different coordinate systems.

Analyze the relationship between forces and motion for rigid bodies using the center of mass and angular momentum theorems to determine and solve equations of motion and calculate necessary constraint forces.
Calculate the mechanical energy of a rigid body system.
Set up the equation of motion for systems with one degree of freedom using the relationship between energy, work, and power.
Analyze the behavior of gyroscopes and rotating machine parts, especially in connection with static and dynamic unbalance.
Explain the fundamentals of Newtonian celestial mechanics.
Apply elementary collision theory to systems of rigid bodies.
Set up and linearize the equation of motion for oscillating systems with one degree of freedom and analyze the behavior of such a free or harmonically excited system.
Analyze problem statements, select suitable methods for their solution, and professionally justify one's own approach.
Starting from the correct physical approach, present the solution path to a problem consistently, making meaningful sketches and diagrams and applying appropriate mathematical methods.
Compare different solution paths, argue results comprehensibly, and check for dimensional correctness and plausibility.
Explain technical content appropriately for the audience, present solution paths understandably, and constructively discuss feedback.
Plan one's own work process, determine priorities, and regularly check progress.

syllabus_topics: Spatial kinematics of the rigid body.
Spatial kinetics of the rigid body: Center of mass theorem, angular momentum theorem, power theorem, work theorem, potential of conservative forces.
Special problems of kinetics: The fast symmetric gyroscope, basic concepts of vibration theory (free/forced vibrations with one degree of freedom), collision processes, fictitious forces.
teaching_methods: Lectures on theoretical foundations and basic tools
Illustration of application with engineering examples
Practical demonstrations in the lecture hall
Practicing what has been learned by independently solving exercise problems

assessment_methods.method: Written and oral examination (calculation problems and questions on theoretical foundations)
Exercise assessment (attendance, participation, homework, and tests)

assessment_rules: The examination consists of written and oral parts, including calculation problems and questions on theoretical foundations. The exercise can be assessed by attendance, participation, homework, and tests. The examination for the lecture can only be taken after successful completion of the exercise.
